info.title: Orgo API
info.description: Launch cloud computers that AI agents can control and interact with. Create workspaces, provision computers, and control them programmatically.

tags.name: Support

tags.name: Clients
tags.description: Run Orgo for your clients from your own app: a workspace and scoped key each, billed to you or to them.

tags.name: Public URLs

tags.name: Computer Actions

tags.name: Screens
tags.description: More than one desktop on a single computer. Each screen is its own X server with its own cursor and window manager, so an agent working on one cannot disturb another.

tags.name: Chat

post.description: Creates a new virtual computer in a workspace. The computer starts automatically after creation. With `ends_in_hours` (1 to 720) a Linux or Windows computer ends: Orgo deletes it when the time is up, running or not, with everything on it. To keep a computer, leave out the end. `on_end` is not a choice: `"delete"` is accepted and changes nothing, and any other value returns `400` (`INVALID_ENDS`). An hourly computer with an end prepays its whole run from credits at launch; the unused part comes back when it stops, is deleted, reaches its end, or its end moves. At the account's computer limit (50 on every plan, plan and hourly computers together), a create with no `billing_mode` is launched by the hour from credits when the credit covers an hour of every hourly computer the account would then have, the new one included. A `402`, `403`, `409` or `503` for credit, the computer limit, the pools, the plan, a size past XL, a taken name, an unbuilt template or `FREE_HOURLY_BUSY` also carries `retryable` and `docs_url`, most carry `next` (the call that fixes it: `method`, `url`, `why`, and `body` when it needs one), and one fixed by adding credit carries `add_credit_url`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: For an hourly launch: a UUID, or any printable key of 1 to 255 characters such as `job-42`. A key that is not a UUID names one launch per UTC day. A retry with the same key launches nothing new and returns the first outcome. The same key with another name, size, OS or workspace returns `409` (`HOURLY_REQUEST_CONFLICT`).

Hourly launches add `BILLING_MODE_REQUIRED`, `INVALID_BILLING_MODE`, `COMPUTE_QUOTE_REQUIRED`, `COMPUTE_REQUEST_ID_REQUIRED`, `STARTER_SIZE_UNSUPPORTED`, and a request for an OS, template, image, snapshot or GPU an hourly launch does not take. `ends_in_hours` adds `INVALID_ENDS` (not a whole number from 1 to 720) and `ENDS_NOT_SUPPORTED` (an `os` other than `linux` or `windows`). An hourly launch on a paid account, or on one Orgo has set to pay from credits, naming a `ram` or `cpu` no hourly size has returns `HOURLY_SIZE_UNAVAILABLE`, with `sizes`.

403.description: The workspace owner's plan does not fund the computer, the request asks for Windows without a license, or you joined through a share link. Codes: `GUEST_RESTRICTED`, `WINDOWS_REQUIRES_SCALE`, `UPGRADE_REQUIRED` (a Free account's create from an API key or an MCP sign-in with no `billing_mode` runs by the hour instead, when hourly can take it), `VM_SLOT_ADDON`, `RAM_ADDON`, `VCPU_ADDON` (the account vCPU pool is used up), `CONTACT_US_FOR_SIZE` (larger than XL, 6 vCPU or 32 GB, which Orgo sets up on request; with `max_cpu` and `max_ram_gb`), `PER_COMPUTER_RAM_CAP`, `PER_COMPUTER_CPU_CAP` (past the 8 vCPU / 64 GB per-computer cap), `CHANGE_PLAN`, `PLAN_LIMIT` (a limit of a plan negotiated with Orgo: a computer count, a per-OS count, the RAM or vCPU pool, or a per-computer RAM or vCPU ceiling), `ACCOUNT_COMPUTER_LIMIT` (the client account's own computer limit), `CLIENT_PRICE_EXCEEDED` (the computer would cost more than the client pays), or none for a grandfathered plan over its limit. Hourly launches add a caller who is not the workspace owner. An expired agent account gets `agent_account_expired`. The quota refusals carry `canManageCapacity` and, where a plan change would fix it, `upgradeTier`. Also: an access check failed: you are not the owner or a member of the workspace, you have Can chat access and the request changes something, or the API key is scoped to another workspace. Hourly launches add `HOURLY_NEEDS_BILLING` (a paid account, from an MCP sign-in or a key without Billing write), `HOURLY_LIMIT` (a free account's one computer on its signup credit alone), `VM_SLOT_ADDON` (the account's computer limit, plan and hourly computers together: past the baseline a computer runs by the hour only with credit for it, and never past the most the account can have; with `computers`, `limit`, `ceiling`, `credit_usd_needed`, `raise_available`, `max_computers` and `computers_used`), and the plan's own refusal (or `PLAN_REFUSED`) for anything but RAM, vCPU or disk room. `RAM_ADDON` and `VCPU_ADDON` carry `hourly_available: true` when the owner, with a credential that may spend credits, can launch the same computer by the hour.

patch.description: Renames a computer, sets its mascot, or sets, moves or clears when it ends. Fields you omit are left alone. Renaming and the mascot need you to own the workspace; the end needs write access to it. The end is `ends_at` (in the future, at most 720 hours away) or `ends_in_hours` (1 to 720), not both; `null` for either takes the end off. Only Linux and Windows computers can have an end. When the end is up the computer is deleted: every end set or moved here deletes it, on a computer whose earlier end would have stopped it (`on_end` `"stop"`) too. `on_end` is not a choice: `"delete"` is accepted and changes nothing (alone, it needs a computer with an end, else `400` `INVALID_ENDS`), and any other value returns `400` (`INVALID_ENDS`). Any change of the end clears `ended_at`. On a running computer that runs by the hour the prepay moves with the end: a later end holds the extra (`402` when the credit cannot cover it plus an hour of your other hourly computers, nothing changed), an earlier end gives back what is past it, and `null` gives back what it has not used and bills it by the hour again, with no prepay. A first end the credit cannot prepay is still set and billed by the hour, with `prepay_warning`. Only the workspace owner prepays, and on a paid plan only signed in or with a key that has full access or Billing write; anyone else with write access still sets the end, nothing more is held, and the answer carries `prepay_warning`. A computer on the plan prepays nothing.

post.description: Starts a `frozen` or `stopped` computer. A `frozen` computer's archived disk is restored and it cold-boots on a host chosen for it, with a new `instance_id` and possibly a new address and ports. A `stopped` computer still on its host is booted there. A `suspended` computer stored off its host is woken from storage onto a host, memory and all, with a new `instance_id`. Starting an already `running` computer returns `{ "success": true }` and changes nothing, except that an end the body sends is set. Accepts the computer UUID or its `instance_id`. The body may set when the computer ends: `ends_in_hours` (1 to 720, counted from when it is running) or `ends_at`, not both; `null` takes any end off. The end is checked as `PATCH /computers/{id}` checks it, before anything starts, and set once the computer is running. When the end is up the computer is deleted. `on_end` `"delete"` with an end is accepted and changes nothing; alone, or any other value, it returns `400` (`INVALID_ENDS`). A computer stopped when an earlier end ran out (`on_end` `"stop"`) comes back with the new end, or with none. A computer that runs by the hour prepays the run to the end under the same rule as PATCH; when the credit is short or the caller may not prepay, the end is still set and billed by the hour, with `prepay_warning`. An end that could not be set never fails the start: the `200` carries `end_not_set`.

post.description: Brings a `suspended` computer back with its memory. On its host it is back in seconds. A computer stored off its host, or whose memory comes back from storage, answers `202`: poll `GET /computers/{id}` or `GET /computers/{id}/suspension` until it is `running` (about a minute). A `running` computer returns `200` and changes nothing, except that an end the body sends is set. Accepts the computer UUID or its `instance_id`. The body may set when the computer ends, as on Start: `ends_in_hours` or `ends_at` (the computer is deleted when it is up), checked before anything resumes and set once the computer is running. A resume still under way (`202`) sets no end and says `end_not_set` with code `STILL_RESUMING`. A suspended computer whose end has passed, but that Orgo is not deleting yet, has its end taken off before it resumes.

Disk growth applies live on Linux; a Windows computer restarts in place to grow its disk. A `mem_gb` change applies live on a Linux computer that supports live memory resize, and restarts any other computer in place. A live change past the vCPU threads the computer booted with (`vcpu_threads`) needs a restart first. Capped by the workspace owner's plan; call `GET /computers/{id}/resize` for the ceiling.

post.description: Runs Bash on Linux or PowerShell on Windows. `timeout` defaults to 200 seconds (maximum 300) on both, and the API waits 30 seconds longer than the command timeout. No background job ID is returned. On Windows the response carries `stdout`, `stderr`, `exit_code`, and `output` (stdout followed directly by stderr) instead of the Linux fields, plus `error` when the command could not run. A Windows command that runs out of time returns `200` with `exit_code` `124`, `error` `"timeout"`, and the output captured so far. On Linux, `?screen=` runs the command on another screen: Orgo prefixes it with `export DISPLAY=:N;` for that screen's display and echoes your command without the prefix. An unknown screen returns `404` and nothing runs.

post.description: Applies the named vault secrets to one running Linux computer: `/root/.orgo-secrets.env`, which `/root/.env` loads, and the own env file of each agent installed there (Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex). Workspace values take precedence over account values. With `remove: true`, takes the names off instead. With `dry_run: true`, changes nothing and answers what either would do. To reach many computers in one call, use `POST /secrets/apply`. Values are never returned.

Applies vault secrets to many running Linux computers in one call, takes them off with `remove: true`, or answers what either would change with `dry_run: true`. With `computer_ids`: exactly those computers. With `workspace_id`: every computer in that workspace. With neither: each name where it is saved, a workspace secret to its workspace and an account secret to every workspace you own. A workspace someone else owns gets account secrets, or loses them on a removal, only when named. Each computer gets what `POST /computers/{id}/secrets/sync` gives it. Four computers at a time. Never wakes a computer. No computer starts after 45 seconds, and no step on a computer starts that could still be running 90 seconds in. The computers that did not start are in `remaining`, and `next` holds the calls that finish the job, each ready to send as it is. A computer that can't be changed is a `failed` or `not_changed` result, never a refusal of the whole call. Values are never returned.

429.description: Nothing was spent. The account made its 10 purchases of the UTC day (`rate_limited`, with `retry_after` and `buy_opens_at`, the next 00:00 UTC). Each purchase from credits and each card payment started counts, paid or not, wherever it was started. Until then `GET /api/billing/residential-data` says `day_limit`. A `rate_limited` without `buy_opens_at` is the API’s own rate limit: wait `retry_after` seconds. Runs an agent on the computer named by `computer_id` until it answers. The agent sees the screen, clicks, types, and runs commands. Request and response follow OpenAI chat completions, plus `computer_id`, `max_steps`, `thread_id`, and an `orgo` block on the response. Leave out `model` to run Computer Use (`orgo-agent`), or `claude-sonnet-5` on an Android computer or when you send only `X-Anthropic-Key`.

Runs bill to the workspace owner's AI credits unless you pay with your own model key: `X-OpenAI-Key` for `orgo-agent`, `X-Anthropic-Key` for the `claude-*` models and `orgo-agent-opus-5.5`. Then no credits are used, `orgo.cost_cents` is `0`, and `orgo.own_key` names the key that paid. A key that can't pay for the model is refused (`400` `own_key_model_mismatch` or `own_key_unsupported`), never ignored. When the provider refuses your key, the error says so: `401` `invalid_own_key`, `429` `own_key_rate_limited`, or `400` `own_key_model_unavailable`. Keys are used for the request only and never stored.

post.description:
Turns the residential proxy on or off for a Linux computer’s Chrome, or gets a new IP. The computer must be running. Turning it on or off restarts Chrome; getting a new IP while it’s on doesn’t.

It draws on the workspace owner’s residential data: what the owner’s plan includes each month, used first, then data bought. This call never spends. With no data left it answers `402` `RESIDENTIAL_DATA_NEEDED`, and the owner buys more with `POST /api/billing/residential-data/buy`. Once the account was added its limit of GB for the UTC day (20 for most accounts, every way together), it answers `429` `RESIDENTIAL_DAILY_LIMIT` with `buy_opens_at` and `daily_gb_limit` instead, to anyone who asks; where data isn’t for sale that is a `409` `residential_daily_limit`. Once the day’s purchases are used it answers `429` `rate_limited` with `buy_opens_at`. Where nobody could add data to the account, anyone who asks gets `503` `RESIDENTIAL_DATA_UNAVAILABLE`. This month’s included data that is waiting to be added (`included.waiting_bytes` on the status) isn’t data left here either.

US IPs only for now: `country` takes `us` and nothing else. To ask about other countries, email contact@orgo.ai.

Some sites can’t be reached through a residential IP: ticketing, video and music streaming, gambling, torrents and speed tests, along with what the network blocks itself, such as banks, government sites and mail ports. Chrome shows ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED for them. Webmail in the browser works. Orgo records the sites a computer reaches this way (the domain, never a path or content), per computer and IP, for 30 days.

value.error: auto_stop_minutes must be a non-negative number

403.description: The free plan, or you can't change this computer.

value.error: Auto-stop is not configurable on the free plan

409.description: The computer is asleep in storage. Wake it first.

example.error: This computer is asleep. Wake it to change its auto-stop setting.

500.description: The setting couldn't be saved.

example.error: Failed to update auto-stop setting

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before asking again.

RateLimitLimit.description: The tightest limit this request counts against.

RateLimitRemaining.description: How many are left of it in this window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until its window starts again.

Template.description: An orgo.ai/v1 template document. Only `api_version` and `template` are required. See the full JSON Schema at GET /template-schema, or the schema guide at https://docs.orgo.ai/guides/templates/schema.

digest.description: Content-addressed SHA-256 digest of the canonical template. Two semantically identical templates always share a digest.

version.description: The version on its own. Present in `GET /templates/{namespace}/{name}`; the curated version list omits it.

auto_build.description: Present only with `?auto_build=true`. `building` while the build is queued or running, `ready` when a golden snapshot for this exact content already exists. Absent when no build could be started; read `build.error`.

build.description: Present only with `?auto_build=true`. What happened to the requested build. The publish itself has succeeded either way.

queued.description: `true` while a build job for this content is queued or running.

job_id.description: Build job ID. Present when a job was queued or found in flight.

state.description: Queue state of the job this request queued.

phase.description: Current job phase. Present when a job was queued or found in flight.

tier.description: Build runner tier. Present when this request queued the job.

ahead.description: Queued jobs across all accounts that will run before this one. Present when this request queued the job.

error.description: Why no build was started. Present only then.

code.description: Machine-readable reason, when one exists, such as `HARDWARE_EXCEEDS_BUILD_RUNNER`.

status.description: `not_built`: no golden snapshot yet, or the last queued build was cancelled. `building`: queued or running. `ready`: launchable. `failed`: see `error`.

build_time_ms.description: Build duration in milliseconds. Present once a queued build has finished.

job_id.description: ID of the newest build job for this version. Present for versions built through the build queue only, as are the fields below.

phase.description: Job phase. `queued` while waiting for a runner, `retrying` while waiting after a failed attempt.

attempts.description: How many times a runner has attempted the job.

finished_at.description: `null` while the job is in flight.

BuildEvent.description: One frame of the build-events SSE stream.

source.description: Origin of the line, e.g. apt, pip, npm, builder.

line.description: A single line of build output.

field.description: Dotted path to the offending field.

details.description: The same list as `errors`, when present.

TemplateRunResponse.description: A short-lived preview computer booted from a template ref: the fleet's create-computer shape plus `desktop_id`, `desktop_api_token`, and `public_host`. Connect to it like any computer; it is auto-reaped.

id.description: The preview's id on the fleet host. `DELETE /templates/run` also accepts it.

desktop_id.description: The preview's identifier in Orgo. Use it as the `instance_id` in connection URLs and pass it to `DELETE /templates/run?id=` to stop the run.

public_host.description: Public hostname of the fleet host the preview was placed on.

desktop_api_token.description: Bearer token for the computer's Desktop API. Equal to `vnc_password`.

ip.description: The computer's address on the host's private network.

api_port.description: Host port serving the Desktop API.

template_ports.description: The template's public `internal` ports mapped to the host ports they were published on. Absent when the template exposes none.

launch.description: How the host launched the preview, without the host's name. Absent when the host does not report it.

cpu.description: `host`, or the CPU model the guest was given.

status.description: `active` for a normal workspace. The product understands `active` and `inactive`. Create stores the value as given; update takes only those two.

icon_url.description: Icon URL for the workspace, or `null` when none is set.

product.description: `orgo`, or `bops` for a workspace the Bops app made.

bops_ws_id.description: Set only on a workspace the Bops app made. `null` otherwise.

owner_tier.description: Subscription tier of the workspace owner. It sets the hardware ceiling for every computer in the workspace.

owner_email.description: Email address of the workspace owner. Returned to every member.

role.description: Your role in the workspace: `owner`, `admin` (can edit), or `member` (Can chat).

member_count.description: People with access to the workspace, counting the owner. Returned by `GET /workspaces` only.

desktops.description: Computers in the workspace, in no guaranteed order. Ephemeral computers are excluded. Each entry is the stored computer record with credential fields removed, plus `permissions`. Treat fields not documented here as internal.

owner_name.description: Name of the workspace owner, or `null` when the owner has not set one.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace the computer belongs to. Returned by `POST /computers`; `GET /computers/{id}` returns it as `project_id`.

os.description: Operating system. `ios` is a physical handset rather than a virtual computer.

ram.description: RAM in GB. `10` or `12` occurs only on macOS.

status.description: Current status. `suspending` while a suspend is being saved, `resuming` while a resume brings it back from storage.

url.description: Base URL of the computer's own API on the host that runs it, as `http://<host>:<port>`. Plain HTTP, and reachable only from inside Orgo's network. It is not a dashboard link and not an endpoint you can call. Use `connection_url` from your own code.

instance_id.description: Identifier of the computer's current VM, returned by `POST /computers`. It changes when the computer is started from archive or woken from storage, so use `id` to refer to the computer. `null` while it has no host (`frozen`, or asleep in storage).

hostname.description: Same-origin host for the computer's connection endpoints: `www.orgo.ai`. Empty while the computer has no instance id, such as when it is `frozen` or asleep in storage.

connection_url.description: Same-origin connection base (https://www.orgo.ai/desktops/{instance_id}). Append /ws/websockify, /ws/terminal, or /ws/audio for WebSocket endpoints; HTTP Desktop API calls go to https://www.orgo.ai/api/desktops/{instance_id}/proxy/{endpoint}.

vnc_password.description: VNC / WebSocket Bearer token. Rotates on restart, on start, and on a RAM resize, so do not persist it. `null` when you have Can chat access to the workspace, when a restricted key lacks Control write, for an MCP sign-in or a computer's identity token, while the computer is locked, while its password is being changed, or when the stored credential cannot be decrypted.

project_id.description: ID of the parent workspace, under its older name. `POST /computers` returns it as a deprecated alias of `workspace_id`; `GET /computers/{id}` returns only this name.

fly_instance_id.description: The instance id under its legacy name. The same value `POST /computers` returns as `instance_id`. `GET /computers/{id}` returns only this name. It changes when the computer is started from archive or woken from storage, so use `id`. `null` while it has no host (`frozen`, or asleep in storage).

private_screens.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`. `true` when the computer's workspace keeps screens private, so the Orgo dashboard keeps the screen covered until someone chooses to show it.

instance_details.description: The computer's placement and connection record: `provider`, `id`, `name`, `webUrl`, `vncHost`, `vncPort`, `apiPort`, `serverAddress`, `resolution`, and `fromPool`, plus `hypervisor` and `templateTerminals` when they apply. `GET /computers/{id}` and the workspace endpoints remove every field whose name contains `password`, `secret`, `token`, `api_key`, or `authorized_keys`, in any letter case and at any depth.

hardware.description: What the computer runs on, from its current VM's launch record. `GET /computers/{id}` always returns it, `null` when the host has not reported a launch record for the computer's current VM. `POST /computers` returns it, with `launch`, only when the host reports how it launched the computer.

host_cpu.description: The host's CPU, or `null` when the launch record does not name it.

cpu_model.description: `host`, or the named CPU model the guest was given.

qemu.description: The QEMU version that ran the computer.

fallback.description: Set when the launch could not do what it was asked and fell back, such as a resume that cold-booted because the CPU differed.

device_tag.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`. The Device ID Orgo prints on a physical device (or, for a macOS VM, on the Mac it runs on). `null` for a VM on Orgo's servers. Read-only.

asleep.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`. Where a `suspended` computer is. `null` when it is not suspended.

where.description: `host`: resumes in seconds. `storage`: off its host; Start, Resume or any action wakes it in about a minute.

reason.description: Why it was put to sleep in storage, when known.

waking.description: Set while a wake is running.

wake_error.description: Why the last wake failed, when it did.

suspension.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`. The current suspension of a `suspended`, `suspending` or `resuming` computer. `null` otherwise, or when nothing is recorded.

saving.description: `true` while its storage copy is still being saved. It can be resumed or deleted meanwhile.

region.description: Region of its storage copy, such as `nyc`.

launch.description: Returned by `POST /computers` alongside `hardware`, when the host reports how it launched the computer: the host's launch record for the new computer, without the host's name or the source its state was restored from.

resolution.description: Display resolution in `WIDTHxHEIGHTxDEPTH` format. Returned by `POST /computers`.

gpu_downgraded.description: Returned by `POST /computers` only, present and `true` when you asked for a `gpu` and a CPU computer was created instead.

warning.description: Present only alongside `gpu_downgraded`, explaining the downgrade.

lock.description: Returned by Get computer. Set only on a Mac, iPhone, or Android phone that Orgo locked because its account is over its plan's capacity: `reason` (`over_capacity`), `locked_at`, and `cap` (how many computers the plan allows). `null` otherwise.

ends_at.description: When the computer ends: Orgo deletes it then, running or not, with everything on it (or, for `on_end` `"stop"`, stops it). `null` when it never ends. `POST /computers` always returns it; `GET /computers/{id}` too. A computer an earlier end stopped keeps it beside `ended_at`.

on_end.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`, and by `POST /computers` when you sent `ends_in_hours` or `on_end`. What happens at the end, read only: `"delete"` (deleted at `ends_at`, as every end set now is), `"stop"` (an end set before every end deleted the computer: stopped at `ends_at`, deleted 7 days later unless it is started), or `null` with no end.

ended_at.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`. When Orgo stopped the computer because its time ran out, or marked it ended if it was already off. `null` when it has not ended. Starting or resuming the computer clears it.

deletes_at.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`. When Orgo deletes the computer: `ends_at` for `on_end` `"delete"`, or 7 days after `ended_at` for an `on_end` `"stop"` computer that has ended. `null` otherwise.

prepaid_until.description: A computer that runs by the hour and is running out a prepaid end: when its prepaid run ends. This is `ends_at`, unless someone who may not prepay moved the end later. `null` for an hourly computer with no prepay, a stopped one, and any computer on a plan. `GET /computers/{id}` always returns it; `POST /computers` only for an hourly create with `ends_in_hours`.

prepaid_cents.description: Alongside `prepaid_until`: what is held from your credits for the prepaid run, in cents, rounded to the nearest cent. `null` when `prepaid_until` is.

ends_warning.description: Returned by `POST /computers` only, when you sent `ends_in_hours` and the computer was made without an end: `This computer can’t have an end, so it keeps running until you stop it.` or `The computer was made, but its end could not be saved, so it keeps running until you stop it.` Do not retry the create.

out_of_memory.description: Returned by `GET /computers/{id}`. When the computer last ran out of memory and its system stopped a program. `null` until that has happened.

kills_24h.description: Programs it stopped in the last 24 hours.

Computer.description: A computer. No single response carries every field: `POST /computers` returns `workspace_id`, `project_id`, `instance_id`, `fly_instance_id`, and the connect fields, plus `hardware` and `launch` when the host reports them, and `ends_at` (with `on_end` when you sent `ends_in_hours` or `on_end`, and `prepaid_until` and `prepaid_cents` for an hourly create with an end); `GET /computers/{id}` returns `project_id`, `project_name`, `permissions`, `fly_instance_id`, the connect fields, `private_screens`, `hardware`, `device_tag`, `asleep`, `suspension`, `lock`, and the end and prepay fields (`ends_at`, `on_end`, `ended_at`, `deletes_at`, `prepaid_until`, `prepaid_cents`); a computer embedded in a workspace carries the stored row. Each operation's example shows what that operation returns.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace to create the computer in

name.description: Computer name, 80 characters at most. Must be unique within the workspace.

os.description: Operating system. Omitted, you get `linux`. Any other value returns `400`. `windows` needs a Scale plan or a Windows computer bought on your plan, otherwise it returns `403` with code `WINDOWS_REQUIRES_SCALE`. `ios` is a physical handset rather than a virtual computer. Every value other than `linux` only succeeds where the fleet has a host that supports it, otherwise create returns `422` with code `OS_UNAVAILABLE`.

cpu.description: vCPU cores. Omitted, it follows the RAM: 4 GB gets 1, 8 GB gets 2, 16 GB gets 4, 32 GB gets 6, 64 GB gets 8. With a `template_ref`, the template's vCPU, never below that. `8` returns `403` (`CONTACT_US_FOR_SIZE`) unless Orgo has set your account up for computers past XL. `16` is above the 8 vCPU per-computer cap and returns `403` (`PER_COMPUTER_CPU_CAP`). Above what the account vCPU pool has left returns `403` (`VCPU_ADDON`). `0` is read as 1. Ignored for `ios`.

ram.description: RAM in GB. Omitted, you get 4, or 10 for `macos`: a create from an API key, the SDKs, the CLI or MCP that names neither `ram` nor `cpu` (and no `template_ref`) gets 4 GB and 1 vCPU. The same create from the dashboard gets a Medium (8 GB, 2 vCPU) when the plan has room for one, and a computer launched by the hour with no size is a Medium. A `macos` computer is always 10: any other value returns `400` with code `MACOS_RAM_FIXED`. `10` with any other `os` returns `400`. `64` returns `403` (`CONTACT_US_FOR_SIZE`) unless Orgo has set your account up for computers past XL. Capped by the workspace owner's plan.

disk_size_gb.description: Disk size in GB. Omit to use template sizing or the owner plan birth size (40 GB on current paid plans). Your plan and unused storage add-ons determine the ceiling, up to 300 GB on current plans. A 150 GB plan ceiling does not include a free 300 GB disk.

resolution.description: Display resolution in `WIDTHxHEIGHTxDEPTH` format. Omitted, `1280x720x24`, or `1920x1080x24` for `macos`. With a `template_ref`, omitting it keeps the template's own resolution.

gpu.description: vGPU slice to attach: `2q` (2 GB VRAM) or `4q` (4 GB VRAM). `"none"`, `""`, `false`, and `"false"` are treated as omitted; any other value returns `400`. Linux only: combining it with another `os` returns `400` with code `GPU_REQUIRES_LINUX`. Omitted, you get a CPU-only computer. If no GPU host can take the create, it either returns `503` with code `GPU_HOST_UNAVAILABLE` or falls back to a CPU computer, and the `201` body then carries `gpu_downgraded` and `warning`.

template_ref.description: Launch from a template's golden snapshot instead of a base image. Format `namespace/name@version`, e.g. `system/claude-code@1.0.0` (curated) or `default/my-template@1.0.0` (your own). The hardware fields above override the template's defaults. The template's build must be `ready`.

billing_mode.description: How the computer is paid for. `plan` counts against the owner's plan, and `monthly` is the same as `plan`. `hourly` runs it by the hour from credits. Any other value returns `400` (`INVALID_BILLING_MODE`). Omitted, the create uses the plan, except as below. Free accounts run hourly computers, a Medium only. On a paid plan the plan comes first: a computer that fits the plan's vCPU and RAM uses the plan, and `hourly` for it returns `409` (`FITS_PLAN`); one past them can run by the hour, and a plan create refused for that room carries `hourly_available: true`. Hourly is for the workspace owner only, Linux or Windows, with no `gpu`, `image` or `snapshot`, and only a starter `template_ref`. On a paid account it needs a person signed in or a key with full access or Billing write, else `403` (`HOURLY_NEEDS_BILLING`). Without a quote, Orgo quotes the size `ram` and `cpu` name at its listed hourly price, or a Medium when they name none; on a paid account a size no hourly offer has returns `400` (`HOURLY_SIZE_UNAVAILABLE`). Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (a UUID, or any printable key of 1 to 255 characters such as `job-42`, which names one launch per UTC day) so a retry returns the same computer. Without enough credit it returns `402` (`insufficient_credit`). Omitted means `hourly` for an unclaimed agent account, for an account Orgo has set to pay for every computer from credits when the create is one hourly can take, and for a Free account's create from an API key or an MCP sign-in that hourly can take (instead of `403` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`). At the account's computer limit (50 on every plan, plan and hourly computers together), a create with no `billing_mode` is launched by the hour when the credit covers an hour of every hourly computer, the new one included, and hourly can take the computer; `plan` there returns `403` (`VM_SLOT_ADDON`).

ends_in_hours.description: When the computer ends, in whole hours after the create: 1 to 720 (30 days). Omitted or `null`: it never ends. Linux and Windows only, else `400` (`ENDS_NOT_SUPPORTED`); any other value returns `400` (`INVALID_ENDS`). When the time is up Orgo deletes the computer, running or not, with everything on it. To keep a computer, leave it out. A computer on the plan prepays nothing. An hourly computer with an end prepays its whole run from credits at launch, always leaving an hour of your other hourly computers that are not prepaid; when the credit is short the create returns `402` with `needed_cents` and `available_cents` and makes nothing.

on_end.description: Not a choice: a computer with an end is deleted when its time is up, running or not, with everything on it. `"delete"` is accepted and changes nothing, with an end or without; omitted or `null` is the same. Any other value, `"stop"` included, returns `400` (`INVALID_ENDS`): `A computer with an end is deleted when its time is up. To keep a computer, leave out the end.`

compute_quote_id.description: With `billing_mode: "hourly"`: a quote from `POST /api/billing/compute`. Omitted, Orgo makes one at the listed price. Sent without `hourly`, returns `400` (`BILLING_MODE_REQUIRED`).

compute_request_id.description: With `billing_mode: "hourly"`: a UUID naming this launch, so a retry with it reads the first outcome. Omitted, the `Idempotency-Key` names the launch, else it gets a new one. Sent without `hourly`, returns `400` (`BILLING_MODE_REQUIRED`).

button.description: Which button to press. Any other value falls back to `left` without an error.

double.description: Double-click instead of single-clicking. A double-click always uses the left button, so `button` has no effect when this is set. The response still echoes the `button` you sent.

modifiers.description: Keys held down for the duration of the click. Use `shift` to extend a selection, `ctrl` to add to one. Optional: omit for a plain click. One to four of `ctrl` (alias `control`), `alt` (alias `option`), `shift`, and `super` (aliases `cmd`, `meta`, `win`). An unrecognised name rejects the whole request rather than dropping one modifier and performing a different gesture. Cannot be combined with `double` or with `repeat` above 1. The response echoes the names normalised, so `option` comes back as `alt`.

repeat.description: Number of clicks in rapid succession, so `3` is a triple-click. Optional. Values of 1 or below behave as a single click, and a value above 10 is refused with `400`. The repeat is counted on the computer, so the gap between presses stays under the toolkit's multi-click threshold no matter how slow the network is. Cannot be combined with `modifiers`.

MouseMoveRequest.description: Where to move the pointer. Both coordinates are required non-negative integers; anything else returns `400`. Any other field is ignored.

x.description: X coordinate, in pixels from the left edge.

y.description: Y coordinate, in pixels from the top edge.

DragRequest.description: On Linux the drag always uses the left button. There is no speed setting. Each coordinate must be a non-negative integer: `0` is a valid coordinate, and a missing, negative, or non-integer coordinate is rejected with `400`.

start_x.description: X coordinate the drag starts at, in pixels from the left edge. A non-negative integer.

start_y.description: Y coordinate the drag starts at, in pixels from the top edge. A non-negative integer.

end_x.description: X coordinate the drag ends at, in pixels from the left edge. A non-negative integer.

end_y.description: Y coordinate the drag ends at, in pixels from the top edge. A non-negative integer.

text.description: Text to type. Unicode is supported. Not validated: omitting it types the empty string and still returns `200`.

delay_ms.description: Delay between keystrokes, in milliseconds. Omitted or `0`, 12 is used. The API waits at most 30 seconds for the typing to finish; longer text returns `503` with `code: "ECONNABORTED"`, and the text may be only partly typed.

key.description: Key or key combination (e.g., Enter, Tab, ctrl+c, alt+F4). On an iPhone: home, app_switcher, Return, BackSpace, space.

x.description: X coordinate to move the pointer to before scrolling, in pixels from the left edge. The pointer is moved before every scroll, so omitting this warps it to `x = 0` and scrolls whatever is under that point. Always send it.

y.description: Y coordinate to move the pointer to before scrolling, in pixels from the top edge. The pointer is moved before every scroll, so omitting this warps it to `y = 0` and scrolls whatever is under that point. Always send it.

direction.description: Scroll direction. Optional. Omitting it scrolls down, and so does any value other than the exact string `up`.

amount.description: Number of wheel clicks. Optional. Omitting it, or sending `0`, scrolls once. A negative value moves the pointer, scrolls nothing, and still returns `200`.

seconds.description: How long to pause, in seconds. Must be greater than `0` and no more than `60`; fractions are allowed. Missing, `0`, negative, or over 60 returns `400`.

duration.description: Deprecated alias for `seconds`. Read only when `seconds` is absent.

timeout.description: How long the command may run, in seconds, on Linux and Windows alike. Omitted, 200. When sent it is clamped to 1-300: a larger value becomes 300, and `0` or a non-numeric value becomes 10. A Windows command that runs out of time returns `200` with `exit_code` `124` and `error` `"timeout"`.

success.description: `true` whenever the command ran at all, regardless of its exit status. Read `exit_code`.

command.description: Echo of the command you sent. With `?screen=`, the `DISPLAY` prefix Orgo adds is left out.

output.description: Combined stdout and stderr, joined by a newline when both are non-empty.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, or `-1` when it was killed by a signal, including by the timeout.

timeout.description: How long the code may run, in seconds. Always clamped to 1-300: a larger value becomes 300, and `0` or a non-numeric value becomes 10. Out-of-range values are never rejected.

success.description: `true` only when the interpreter exited zero. Code that raises returns `200` with `success: false`.

output.description: Combined stdout and stderr. An uncaught exception's traceback arrives here.

timeout.description: Always `false`, even when the code was killed by the timeout. Infer a timeout from `success: false` with truncated output.

error.description: Always `null` on a `200`, including when the code raises.

error_type.description: Always `null` on a `200`. It never carries a Python exception class.

success.description: Always `true` on a `200`. A failed action is an error status.

details.description: Echo of what was performed. Its fields depend on the action.

desktop_id.description: Computer the file is associated with, or `null` when it is not tied to one.

storage_key.description: Where it is kept in workspace storage.

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes, as a decimal string such as `"102400"`. The value is a 64-bit integer, so it is serialized as a string. Parse it before doing arithmetic. `null` when no size was recorded.

source.description: How the file entered the workspace.

file.description: The stored file record: every column of the row, plus `workspace_id`.

project_id.description: The same value as `workspace_id`, under the workspace's older name. Read `workspace_id` in new code.

user_id.description: ID of the account that uploaded the file.

storage_key.description: Internal object-storage key. It is not a URL and cannot be fetched directly. Use the download endpoint to get a signed URL.

path.description: Absolute path of the file on the computer, such as `/root/Desktop/results.txt` or `C:\Users\Public\results.txt`.

url.description: Signed download URL. Works for one hour.

Error.description: The base error body. Every failure carries `error`; individual endpoints add the fields named in the schemas below.

code.description: Machine-readable reason. Present on the failures that define one, absent otherwise.

id.description: Screen identifier. The boot screen is always `default`.

display.description: X display this screen runs on.

default.description: True for the screen the computer boots with. It cannot be destroyed.

width.description: Width in pixels. Omitted, the screen matches the boot screen.

height.description: Height in pixels. Omitted, the screen matches the boot screen.

ScreenRequest.description: Size for a new screen. Send both dimensions or neither: if either is missing or zero, both fall back to the size of the boot screen and the value you did send is discarded without an error.

ScopeError.description: A workspace-scoped API key was used against a workspace it is not scoped to. Use an account-wide key, or a key scoped to the workspace you are addressing.

key_workspace_id.description: The workspace the key is scoped to.

target_workspace_id.description: The workspace the request tried to reach.

QuotaError.description: The request was refused by the plan the workspace owner is on rather than by ownership. See https://www.orgo.ai/#pricing for what each plan includes.

code.description: Machine-readable reason. Values this API emits: `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, `DESKTOP_LIMIT`, `VM_SLOT_ADDON`, `RAM_ADDON`, `PER_COMPUTER_RAM_CAP`, `VCPU_ADDON`, `PER_COMPUTER_CPU_CAP`, `DISK_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `disk_exceeds_quota`, `WINDOWS_REQUIRES_SCALE`, `GUEST_RESTRICTED`, `NOT_A_MEMBER`, `CHANGE_PLAN`, `PLAN_LIMIT`, `upgrade_required`.

upgradeTier.description: The plan that would allow the request.

canManageCapacity.description: True when you own the workspace and can raise the limit yourself.

max_ram_gb.description: On a RAM refusal from resize: the largest RAM a live resize can reach for this computer.

max_disk_gb.description: On a storage refusal: the largest disk this computer may have.

UpstreamError.description: A failure the computer itself returned, relayed with the computer's own status.

request_id.description: Correlation id for this failure. The server logged the failure under it, so quote it in a support report.

upstream_status.description: The status the computer returned. Mirrors the status of this response.

InternalError.description: An unexpected failure. Retrying is reasonable; if it persists, quote `request_id`.

request_id.description: Present on failures raised by a route that talks to a computer. Absent on the others.

UnreachableError.description: The computer could not be reached. The diagnostic fields, present on the command endpoints, say how far the request got.

error.example: Could not reach the desktop. Try again in a moment.

code.description: The socket-level error code, or `network_error` when none was reported.

vm_status.description: The computer's recorded status when the request failed.

desired_status.description: The status the computer was being driven towards, when one was recorded.

host_reachable.description: Whether the host running the computer answered.

desktop_api_reachable.description: Whether the computer's own API answered.

hint.description: What to do next, given the two reachability results.

TimeoutError.description: The command ran past the time allowed for it and was aborted. Raise `timeout` on the request, up to 300 seconds.

error.example: The command exceeded the allowed time and was aborted.

BackendError.description: The fleet could not satisfy the request right now. Retry.

retryable.description: Present and `true` on the capacity failures a later retry can clear.

TemplateError.description: A failure from the template registry, relayed with the registry's own status and code.

code.description: Machine-readable reason, when the registry supplied one.

details.description: Per-field validation errors, or the raw upstream body when it was not JSON.

FilePlacedResponse.description: Returned instead of `FileUploadResponse` when the request carried `destPath`. No file record is created.

placedIn.description: The folder the file was placed in: your `destPath` with surrounding whitespace trimmed, or `the desktop` when you sent `desktop`. The file name is not appended.

BotMascot.description: The computer's mascot appearance. Every field is optional; an omitted field falls back to the app default. An unrecognised field or value is dropped rather than rejected, so a client one release ahead of the API degrades one field instead of failing the whole write.

ResizeLimits.description: The values a resize on this computer will accept, computed from the workspace owner's plan plus the add-on capacity their other computers have not already claimed.

base_disk_gb.description: Disk per computer included in the owner's plan.

blocks.description: Storage add-on blocks the owner has bought.

add_on_gb.description: Storage those blocks are worth, in GB.

max_disk_gb.description: Largest `disk_size_gb` a resize will accept for this computer.

max_ram_gb.description: Largest `mem_gb` a live resize will accept. Bounded by the host's boot-memory ceiling and by the RAM the owner's other computers leave in the account's pool, as well as the plan, so it can be lower than the RAM the computer could be created at.

max_bandwidth_mbps.description: Largest `bandwidth_limit_mbps` the workspace owner's plan allows.

addon_ram_gb.description: Pooled RAM add-on the owner has bought, in GB.

addon_vcpu.description: Pooled vCPU add-on the owner has bought.

live_mem_resize.description: `true` when a `mem_gb` change applies without restarting the computer. Absent when the host cannot say, for example when the computer is not running.

hard_max_ram_gb.description: The most RAM this computer can be resized to on its host, whatever the plan allows.

hard_max_cpu.description: The per-computer vCPU ceiling, 8, or lower on a custom plan that sets its own. No add-on lifts it.

self_serve_max_cpu.description: The most vCPU you can resize this computer to on your own: the lower of 6 (XL) and `hard_max_cpu`, or `hard_max_cpu` when `past_xl_allowed` is `true`. Past it, the resize returns `403` (`CONTACT_US_FOR_SIZE`).

self_serve_max_ram_gb.description: The most RAM you can resize this computer to on your own: the lower of 32 (XL) and `hard_max_ram_gb`, or `hard_max_ram_gb` when `past_xl_allowed` is `true`.

past_xl_allowed.description: Whether Orgo has set the workspace owner's account up for computers past XL (more than 6 vCPU or 32 GB).

vcpu_threads.description: The vCPU threads the computer booted with. A live `vcpus` change past this needs a restart first. Absent when the host cannot say, for example when the computer is not running.

hourly.description: Hourly computers that can change size only. Their answer has no `base_disk_gb`, `blocks`, `add_on_gb`, `max_bandwidth_mbps`, `addon_ram_gb` or `addon_vcpu`, and `max_disk_gb` is the current disk.

may_spend.description: Whether you may pick a higher rate.

ScreenResizeRequest.description: The new size. Both dimensions are required here, unlike creating a screen. There is no boot screen to fall back to when the intent is an explicit change.

result.description: On success, such as `{ "success": true }`. A Start that was asked for an end also carries the end fields: `ends_at`, `ended_at`, `deletes_at`, and for an hourly computer `prepaid_until`, `prepaid_cents`, `prepay_returned_cents`, and `prepay_warning`, or `end_not_set` when the end was not set.

error.description: On failure: `error`, `code`, and `status`, plus `retry_after` (seconds) when it says when to try again.

Permissions.description: What your role in the workspace allows.

canUseAgent.description: Whether you may chat with the workspace's agents. `true` for every role, Can chat included.

ResizeUnavailable.description: Returned with `200` instead of `ResizeLimits` for a computer that cannot be resized, such as a physical device or an operating system without resize support. Every ceiling is set to the computer's current size.

ResizeResult.description: The effective configuration after the resize attempt. A dimension that failed to apply comes back with its previous value.

auto_stop_minutes.description: The `auto_stop_minutes` you sent, echoed back. Absent when you did not send it.

connection_rotated.description: `true` when the computer's ports or VNC password changed. Re-fetch `GET /computers/{id}` before reconnecting.

restarted.description: `true` when the resize restarted the computer, `false` when it applied live, `null` when the host does not report it.

identity_changed.description: Connection values the host reports as changed. Empty when nothing changed or the host does not report changes.

results.description: One entry per attempted hardware dimension. Absent when the request included no hardware dimension.

partial.description: `true` when at least one dimension failed. `true` on both `207` and `422`. Absent when the request included no hardware dimension.

c_drive.description: Windows only, after a disk grow: whether drive C: was extended to use it.

restart_required.description: GPU computers only, when `vcpus` or `mem_gb` changed.

price.description: GPU computers only, alongside `restart_required`: `monthly_usd`, `yearly_usd`, `hourly_usd`, and `lines`. Shown, not charged.

running_usd_per_hour.description: Hourly computers only: the rate after the resize.

BuildJob.description: A build queued for a dedicated build runner.

status.description: `queued` while the job waits for a runner, `building` once a runner has claimed it.

ahead.description: Queued jobs across all accounts that will run before this one.

launchOnReady.description: Whether a computer is created when the build is ready. For a job already in flight, that job's setting, not this request's.

computers.description: `limit` and `in_use` count plan computers: how many the plan funds and how many plan computers the account has. Beside them is the account's one computer limit, plan and hourly computers together: `total`, `baseline`, `ceiling`, `can_raise` and `raise_available`.

limit.description: How many plan computers the plan funds.

in_use.description: The plan computers the account has.

total.description: Every computer the account has, plan and hourly, running or stopped. `null` when it could not be read.

baseline.description: 50 on every paid plan, or the account's own number. Past it, new computers run by the hour from credit. `null` when the account has no limit, or it could not be read.

ceiling.description: The most computers the account can have: 999, or its own number when that is higher (up to 9999). `null` when it could not be read.

can_raise.description: `true` when the credit covers going past the baseline now, for a Medium Linux computer by the hour. `null` when the credit could not be read.

raise_available.description: `false` when credit can't raise the limit at all, or it could not be read.

ram_gb.description: The account-wide RAM pool and what its computers use.

vcpu.description: The account vCPU pool and what its computers use. `limit` is `null` when there is no pool limit.

computers.description: Computer slots bought before slots were retired. A purchase adds none.

added.description: What the account has added beyond its plan.

self_serve_cap.description: The most the account may add on its own. Past it, purchases return `403` `capacity_cap`; ask us and we raise it for the account.

can_add.description: How many more computers' worth of each size's memory, vCPU and disk the account may add now, under its cap. It is room, not computers. `0` for `2xl` unless `past_xl_allowed`.

max_per_request.description: The most computers' worth one purchase may add (500).

rates.description: Per-part prices for each term: every shape, and parts on their own, are billed at these.

computer_usd.description: Always `0`: computer slots are no longer sold.
Always `0`: computer slots are no longer sold.

per_computer_max.description: The largest any one computer can be.

past_xl_allowed.description: Whether this account may add computers past XL (over 6 vCPU or 32 GB) itself. Otherwise they are set up on request.

Client.description: A client: a workspace you run for them, with a key scoped to it.

computers.description: Up to 50, newest first. Not on Add a client or List clients.

ChatError.description: The error body of `POST /v1/chat/completions`. Unlike the rest of the API, `error` is an object.

code.description: Machine-readable reason. Branch on this, not on `message`.

param.description: Only on `invalid_messages`: the field that failed, such as `messages[0].content[1]`.

balance_cents.description: Only on `402`: the payer's credit balance, in cents.

limit.description: Only on `rate_limited`: the limit that was reached, `chat_runs_per_minute` or `chat_runs_concurrent`.

retry_after.description: Only on `rate_limited`: seconds until a retry can succeed.

url.description: The link a person opens to claim the account: `https://www.orgo.ai/claim/{token}`. Works once.

code.description: A short code in the form `XXX-XXX-XXX`. Show it to your person so they can check they are claiming the right account, or have them type it at `https://www.orgo.ai/claim`.

expires_at.description: When the link and code stop working (7 days after they were made).

status.description: `unclaimed` until a person claims it, then `claimed`.

expires_at.description: When an unclaimed account expires. `null` once claimed.

claimed_at.description: When a person claimed it, or `null`.

Suspension.description: A computer's suspension: where its memory is and how far saving it has got. No host, bucket or key.

progress.description: 0 to 1 once the size is known (1 once stored), else `null`.

local_only.description: `true` when saving to storage failed and its host kept the memory: it resumes only there.

saving.description: `true` while its storage copy is still being saved.

region.description: Region of its storage copy, such as `nyc`.

SecretsReportTarget.description: One agent the call reached, or would reach. Agents that are not installed are left out.

id.description: The agent: `hermes`, `openclaw`, `codex`, `claude-code`, `opencode`, or `agy`. `agents` for the agent step as a whole.

status.description: `updated`: the agent's file was written. `unchanged`: on an apply, the file did not change; in a preview, none of the names would go in it (each is in `skipped`). `shell`: the agent has no env file and reads `/root/.env`. `cleared`: Orgo's lines for `names` were taken out. `skipped`: the file was left alone (`reason`). A preview (`dry_run: true`) says `would_update` and `would_clear` in place of `updated` and `cleared`.

reason.description: Why a target was skipped. `owner_managed`: a Hermes whose gateway its owner runs on their own setup. `unreadable`: Orgo can't read the file. `write_failed`: Orgo couldn't write it (never in a preview). `state_unreadable`, on `agents`: `/root/.orgo-secrets.agents.json` does not parse, so no agent file was touched.

names.description: The names written, taken out, or that would be.

skipped.description: Names left out of this file. Never a value.

reason.description: `value_format`: the value has a single quote, a backslash, `${`, or a line break of any kind, so it stays out of the agent's file and still reaches `/root/.env`. `reserved` (preview only): the agent keeps its own value for this name, such as Hermes' `HERMES_HOME`, `API_SERVER_` and chat app names, Codex's `CODEX_` names, or OpenClaw's `OPENCLAW_` names.

restart.description: The supervisord program to restart for the change to take effect. `openclaw-gateway` whenever OpenClaw's file changes. `hermes-gateway` when a line leaves Hermes' file: a removal, or an apply that takes out the old line of a value Hermes' file can't hold.

SecretsReport.description: What happened, or would happen, to each agent's env file on the computer. Names, ids and statuses only, never a value. `null` when no report line came back from the computer.

names.description: A removal, or its preview: what happened to each name on this computer. `cleared` when at least one copy was taken out, `kept` when a copy stays and none was taken out, `none` when there was no copy. A preview says `would_clear` and `would_keep`. `kept_in` says where a copy stays.

kept_in.description: A removal, or its preview: where a copy of a name stays. `dotenv` is a line in `/root/.env` from when the computer was created that does not hold your current vault value. An agent id is a line in that agent's file that was changed on the computer, or a file Orgo could not read or write.

computer_id.description: The computer's UUID when Orgo could read the computer, else the id as you sent it.

name.description: The computer's name. `null` when it is not known, such as for a computer that was not found.

workspace_id.description: The computer's workspace. `null` when it is not known.

reason.description: On `not_changed` and `failed`: why, as a sentence you can show people, such as `Asleep. Not changed.` or `Computer not found.`

report.description: On `applied`, `removed`, and `previewed`: what the computer reported. `null` when no report came back.

error.description: Which limit, in plain words, and when to try again.

example.error: Too many API requests this minute (120 a minute on your plan). Try again in 12 seconds.

at.description: When it started, in milliseconds since 1970.

output.description: What the last step to run handed on.

waiting.description: The step it waits at: id, title, asks (a person’s), agent and until (another agent’s).

stop.description: Why it stopped, and the one thing that fixes it.

fix.description: The one thing that fixes it: action (reconnect, edit, secrets, setup, credits, check) and what it needs.

CreateWorkflow.description: describe or lines, one of the two.

describe.description: What it does, in plain words. Orgo drafts the steps.

lines.description: The steps themselves, one JSON object per line (https://www.orgo.ai/workflows.md).

time_zone.description: An IANA zone its times are read in, like America/New_York.

say.description: The same, short, for a person.

lines.description: version_conflict: the newest lines, to merge into.

scheduled.description: False: on, with a time to come, and nothing set to start it then. Null: not known now.

settings.description: Only the names sent change; "" or null takes one out.

computer.description: The computer its steps run on (its UUID, from List workspaces or Get workspace); null takes it off.

on.description: Whether its start runs it. It is on only while it can run.

version.description: Send it as If-Match on a write.

lines.description: The workflow, one JSON object per step, the start first (https://www.orgo.ai/workflows.md).

settings.description: What it asks for once, name to value.

to_fix.description: What still has to be done before it can run, in the person’s words. Empty: ready.

step.description: The step it is on (empty: the whole workflow).

turned_off.description: This write left it unable to run, so it was turned off.

dropped.description: What of the lines sent was left out or rewritten.

label.description: The part of the hostname before the base domain.

port.description: The port on the computer the URL serves.

protected.description: `true` when visitors must enter a password first.

disabled.description: Present and `true` only when Orgo support turned the URL off. It is not served and cannot be changed or removed.

enabled.description: `false` when public URLs are off for your account or this computer cannot have them.

reason.description: Why `enabled` is `false`, when the computer is the reason.

limit.description: Most public URLs this computer can have. Negative means no limit.

account_limit.description: Most public URLs the workspace owner can have across all their computers. Negative means no limit.

account_used.description: How many the workspace owner has.

port.description: The port your app listens on inside the computer. Not 22, 3389, 5900 to 5999, 6080 to 6099, 8080 or 9000: the computer uses those itself.

name.description: The start of the address. Orgo adds 4 characters after it, so `cool-thing` becomes `cool-thing-x7k2`. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Omit it and Orgo picks one.

label.description: Older name for `name`, read the same way. To get back an address the workspace owner removed in the last 30 days, send its full label here, for example `cool-thing-x7k2`. Send `name` or `label`, not both.

port.description: Serve another port on the computer.

password.description: 4 to 64 printable ASCII characters, case sensitive, no space at the start or end. `null` removes the password.
The password, or `null` when anyone can open the URL.

cookie.description: The cookie the password form sets. Send it to open the URL without the form. `null` when anyone can open the URL.

ResidentialProxyStatus.description: Which route the computer’s Chrome leaves through, its exit IP, and the account’s residential data. `state`, `billing`, `quota.counted_at` and `quota.this_computer_bytes` are present on a Linux computer set to the residential route, and never on a Bops computer. `included` is present when the owner’s plan includes data.

mode.description: The computer's browser route. `residential` is the default. `custom` is your own proxy, set with `POST /api/computers/{id}/egress/upstream` (see [Browser networking](/guides/browser-networking#bring-your-own-proxy)); with it, turning the relay on uses your proxy, not a residential IP.

proxy_on.description: Whether Chrome goes through the relay. It is also true on a `custom` route, which is not a residential IP, so read `mode` too.

exit_ip.description: The address websites see from Chrome, as last read. Null while the relay is off or before it was read.

country.description: The exit country. Only `us` for now.

computer_blocked_reason.description: Why this computer can’t use a residential IP whatever data the account has: a Bops computer, a dedicated IP that is on, or residential IPs paused for this computer. Absent when nothing stops it. Buying data does not help while it is set.

state.description: Where the account’s data stands. `none`: the account has never had any. `ok`: some left. `low`: under 0.25 GB left. `buying`: a purchase is still finishing. `out`: none left, so Chrome can’t load pages until there is more. Present on a Linux computer set to the residential route, and never on a Bops computer.

quota.description: The workspace owner’s residential data. Every computer of the workspace owner draws on it.

granted_bytes.description: All the residential data the account has had: what it bought and what its plan included. This month’s included data counts in full from the start of the month, except while it can’t be added (data can’t be added right now, or the account reached its limit for the day): then what hasn’t been added yet is left out (`included.waiting_bytes`). `granted_bytes` less `used_bytes` is what is left.

used_bytes.description: Data used: the network’s count at `counted_at`, plus what the account’s computers reported since. An estimate between counts.

remaining_bytes.description: Data left. At 0, Chrome stops loading pages and never falls back to the data center IP. While data can’t be added, or once the account reached its limit for the day, this month’s included data not added yet is left out, and `state` follows what has been added.

counted_at.description: When the network last counted the account’s use. Null before the first count. Present with `state`.

this_computer_bytes.description: About how much this computer has used, as the computer reports it. Present with `state`.

billing.description: Whether more data can be bought now. Present with `state`. It carries no balance: [Get residential data](/api-reference/account/residential-data) has that, for the owner.

price_cents_per_gb.description: The price of 1 GB, in cents. Null while it is not for sale.

can_buy.description: The caller can buy data now.

buy_blocked_reason.description: Why `can_buy` is false, the first that applies in this order. Null when `can_buy` is true. `unavailable`: nobody can add data to this account right now: for example the network has none to add, residential data is blocked for the account, the account is being deleted, or a refund or dispute isn’t settled. Paying, adding credit or a computer won’t help, so try later. A member reads it too. `daily_data_limit`: the account was added its limit of GB for the UTC day (`daily_gb_limit`), every way together: purchases from credits, card payments, auto-buy and the plan’s included data. More can be added at `buy_opens_at`, the next 00:00 UTC, and nothing lifts it sooner. A member reads it too. `day_limit`: the account made its 10 purchases of the UTC day. Each purchase from credits and each card payment started counts, paid or not. Buy again at `buy_opens_at`, the next 00:00 UTC. A member reads it too, since the owner can’t buy either. `not_owner`: only the workspace owner buys data, signed in or with an account-wide key that has full access or Billing write. `not_paying`: no paid plan and no credit bought. Starting credit alone can’t buy residential data: pay by card signed in to Orgo, or add credit first. Once the account has paid, its whole balance pays, starting credit included. `credit_short`: the credits don’t cover 1 GB.

payer.description: The caller is the workspace owner, signed in or with an account-wide key that has full access or Billing write: the one who pays for this computer’s data. False for a member and a narrower key.

card_available.description: The workspace owner, signed in to Orgo, can pay for data by card here, also with no paid plan and no credit bought (`not_paying`). Always false with an API key, which can’t pay by card, and for anyone else. `can_buy` and `buy_blocked_reason` still say whether a purchase can go now.

buy_opens_at.description: With `day_limit` or `daily_data_limit` only: when a purchase can go again, the next 00:00 UTC.

daily_gb_limit.description: With `daily_data_limit` only. The account’s limit of residential data added a UTC day, in whole GB: 20 for most accounts. Every way data is added counts together: purchases from credits, card payments, auto-buy and the plan’s included data.

included.description: The data the owner’s plan includes this UTC month, used before data bought. Absent on a plan with none, such as Free, and on a plan on a trial until the trial ends.

gb_per_month.description: GB the plan includes each month: 1 on Starter, 5 on Growth, 20 on Scale and Enterprise.

used_bytes.description: Used of it this UTC month. An estimate between counts.

resets_at.description: When it comes back in full: 00:00 UTC on the 1st of next month, on the plan the account has then. What is left does not roll over. If the plan ends, pauses or switches first, the amount follows that plan from that day.

waiting_bytes.description: This month’s included data not added to the account yet that can’t be added now: while data can’t be added, or once the account reached its limit for the day. It is not in `remaining_bytes`, and not used either. Absent while there is none.

status.description: `pending`: the credits are held, not spent. `added`: charged. `returned`: not added, and the credits went back.

auto.description: Bought by auto-buy, not by hand.

left_bytes.description: Data left: bought, and this month’s included data. As the network last counted it, less what the computers reported since, never below zero. An estimate between counts. While data can’t be added (`buy_blocked_reason` `unavailable`), or once the account reached its limit for the day (`daily_data_limit`), this month’s included data not added yet is left out: it is `included.waiting_bytes` instead.

counted_at.description: When the network last counted the account’s use. Null before the first count.

price_cents.description: The price of 1 GB, in cents. Null while it is not for sale.

can_buy.description: The account can buy data now.

buy_blocked_reason.description: Why `can_buy` is false, the first that applies in this order. Null when `can_buy` is true. `unavailable`: nobody can add data to this account right now: for example the network has none to add, residential data is blocked for the account, the account is being deleted, or a refund or dispute isn’t settled. Paying, adding credit or a computer won’t help, so try later. `daily_data_limit`: the account was added its limit of GB for the UTC day (`daily_gb_limit`), every way together: purchases from credits, card payments, auto-buy and the plan’s included data. More can be added at `buy_opens_at`, the next 00:00 UTC, and nothing lifts it sooner. The limit is on adding data, not using it. `no_computer`: no Linux computer outside Bops for the data to run on, on a free account too. Add one first. `day_limit`: the account made its 10 purchases of the UTC day. Each purchase from credits and each card payment started counts, paid or not. Buy again at `buy_opens_at`, the next 00:00 UTC. `not_paying`: no paid plan and no credit bought. Starting credit alone can’t buy residential data: pay by card signed in to Orgo, or add credit first. Once the account has paid, its whole balance pays, starting credit included. `credit_short`: the credits don’t cover 1 GB. `needs_billing`: this key has no Billing write, and nothing else stops the buy. Use a key with Billing write, or Orgo itself. Any other reason stays as it is, since a key with Billing write would meet it too.

buy_opens_at.description: With `day_limit` or `daily_data_limit` only: when a purchase can go again, the next 00:00 UTC.

available_cents.description: The account’s credits, in cents, when they were read.

terms_accepted.description: The account has bought before, and with that accepted the Residential IPs terms. Auto-buy buys nothing while this is false. Absent while it is not for sale.

card_available.description: A person signed in to Orgo can pay for data by card in Plan and billing, also with no paid plan and no credit bought (`not_paying`). False with an API key, which can’t pay by card. `can_buy` and `buy_blocked_reason` still say whether a purchase can go now. Absent while it is not for sale.

max_gb.description: The most one purchase can add now, in whole GB: at most 100, and at most `daily_gb_left` where the account has a daily limit, so 20 or less for most accounts. Less while the network has less to add, and 0 while nothing can be added. It follows the network’s newest count, so read it just before you buy. Absent while it is not for sale.

daily_gb_limit.description: The account’s limit of residential data added a UTC day, in whole GB: 20 for most accounts. Every way data is added counts together: purchases from credits, card payments, auto-buy and the plan’s included data. Null where no limit applies. Absent while it is not for sale.

daily_gb_left.description: What `daily_gb_limit` leaves this UTC day, in whole GB. At 0, `buy_blocked_reason` is `daily_data_limit` until `buy_opens_at`, the next 00:00 UTC. Null where no limit applies, or when it couldn’t be read. Absent while it is not for sale.

purchases.description: Newest first, at most 20. Included data is not a purchase.

auto_buy.description: Buying 1 GB from credits when data falls under 0.25 GB. Set by a person in Plan and billing, and only there. It buys nothing until the account has bought once by hand, which accepts the Residential IPs terms (`terms_accepted`).

available.description: It can be turned on now. Absent while residential data is not for sale.

monthly_cap_gb.description: The most it buys in a UTC month, 1 to 100.

price_cents.description: The price of 1 GB the person agreed to. A new price pauses auto-buy until they save it again.

paused_reason.description: Why it is paused. Null when it is not.

bought_this_month_gb.description: GB it bought this UTC month.

included.description: Residential data the plan includes this UTC month, used before data bought. Absent on a plan with none, such as Free, and on a plan on a trial, which includes none until the trial ends (`included_after_trial`).

gb_per_month.description: 1 on Starter, 5 on Growth, 20 on Scale and Enterprise.

used_bytes.description: Used this UTC month, as the network last counted it plus what the computers reported since, never past `gb_per_month`. An estimate between counts.

left_bytes.description: The plan’s data left this month. It can be a little more than `gb_per_month`, as data is added in whole GB, or more after a switch to a smaller plan: all of it is still the plan’s. Not `waiting_bytes`.

waiting_bytes.description: This month’s included data not added to the account yet that can’t be added now: while data can’t be added (`buy_blocked_reason` `unavailable`), or once the account reached its limit for the day (`daily_data_limit`). It is in neither `left_bytes`, and not used either. Absent while there is none.

resets_at.description: When it comes back: the start of the next UTC month, on the plan the account has then. What is left does not roll over. If the plan ends, pauses or switches first, the amount follows that plan from that day.

included_after_trial.description: A plan on a trial includes no residential data until the trial ends: what it will include each UTC month from then. Absent otherwise, and never with `included`.

invalid-key.summary: The key is not one of yours

CommandTimeout.description: The command ran past the time allowed for it and was aborted. Nothing is rolled back: whatever the command did before the abort has happened.

example.error: The command exceeded the allowed time and was aborted.

value.error: internal error

timeout.summary: The registry host did not answer in time

AuthUnavailable.description: Orgo could not verify the credential because of a server-side fault, such as a database outage. Retry after `Retry-After`. Do not rotate the key.

example.error: Service temporarily unavailable. The database is not accepting requests. Retry shortly.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Always `5`.

TrialInactive.description: The computer is a free trial computer whose trial is no longer active, or it is paid for by its own subscription or dedicated purchase and that payment has lapsed.

value.error: Choose a plan to continue.

Forbidden.description: Access denied or plan limit reached

example.error: Access denied

RateLimited.description: Over one of the account's plan rate limits (`rate_limited`): `limit` names it, and `retry_after` and `Retry-After` say how many seconds to wait. Limits are per account, the workspace owner's when the request acts on a computer or a workspace, and set by its plan. See [Account limits and rate limits](/guides/account-limits#plan-rate-limits).
